segments.title: Chương 91: 0091【Thời Thế Hợp Lực】
segments.content:
Chapter 94: When the Time is Right, Heaven and Earth Lend Their Strength

Dorm Room 404.

Jiang Junlai stared blankly at a thick stack of course schedules. He turned his head to Chen Guiliang and said, "The professor giving the lecture this afternoon is named Xu Lai. I heard that he started receiving a state council special allowance more than ten years ago. And he's supposedly a direct disciple of Zhang Dainian and Feng Youlan."

"That's pretty damn impressive," Chen Guiliang said.

Jiang Junlai asked, "Who are Zhang Dainian and Feng Youlan?"

"You just need to know that they're extremely impressive." Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to explain; it wasn't something that could be clarified in just a few words.

Before the semester officially began, the Yuanpei Program had professors giving lectures every day. They were invited by department leaders to coax the freshmen into choosing courses from their respective departments.

Chen Guiliang knew of this Professor Xu Lai from his previous life.

To put it in ancient terms, Xu Lai was currently a "Great Scholar."

In another ten years, after he published his "Ontology of Ren-based Learning," he would directly ascend to the level of a "Grandmaster" in Confucian studies.

Moreover, his set of theories was conducive to the construction of socialist spiritual civilization and was listed among the top ten original theories in the field of Chinese philosophy and social sciences.

The other nine original theories were also the works of titans.

One of those titans, an economics expert, had reportedly swum over from the other shore while hugging a basketball. Well, that titan was also slated to join the faculty at Peking University next year and would even serve as a part-time mentor for the Yuanpei Program.

"Wanna go for a trip to Weiming Lake?"

Deng Chen and Yun Fan from the room across the hall ran over.

Chen Guiliang, organizing his application materials, said, "I'll go another day."

Jiang Junlai glanced over. "Are you really starting a company?"

"Just starting one for fun," Chen Guiliang said.

Deng Chen and Yun Fan didn't say anything, but they were deeply impressed.

Damn, the semester hadn't even officially started yet!

While they were stressing over which courses and clubs to choose, this guy was already starting a company.

Deng Chen glanced at the empty bunk with a suitcase on it. "This senior still hasn't moved in?"

Jiang Junlai said, "I hear he's some kind of immortal, probably off wandering somewhere."

Chen Guiliang slung his backpack over his shoulder. "You guys take your time chatting."

"Wait!"

The four of them set out together, walking about a hundred meters to rent bicycles near Building 28.

Chen Guiliang rode from the South Gate towards the East Gate, having to circle halfway around the Peking University campus.

The other three rode off to rent a camera, planning to take souvenir photos at Weiming Lake and the main gate of Peking University.

Peking University Science Park was currently a massive construction site. Buildings and expansions were going up everywhere this year, and the office areas were temporarily moved and concentrated in the Innovation Center.

Chen Guiliang locked his bike outside and asked for directions all the way to the Incubation Services Department.

"Knock, knock, knock!"

The door was ajar. Chen Guiliang knocked and asked, "Excuse me, may I come in?"

"Come in," someone inside replied.

Perhaps because construction was happening everywhere else, the entire Incubation Services Department was squeezed in here, with several people crowded inside working.

One or two people were busy, while the others were playing on their computers.

"Excuse me, which staff member should I see about applying for a project?" Chen Guiliang asked.

A man in his forties with a receding hairline closed the Minesweeper game on his computer and said, "Come over here. Are your materials ready?"

Chen Guiliang opened his backpack. "They're ready. Please take a look, sir."

The slightly balding man took the documents, glanced at them, and looked up at Chen Guiliang in surprise. "A freshman?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang said.

The man didn't know whether to laugh or cry. He handed the materials back to Chen Guiliang. "You all haven't even officially started the semester, and you're starting a project and a company? Go back and study. Freshman year is the time to build your foundation."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Can't freshmen start companies?"

The man said, "You can, of course. But what can you accomplish as a freshman?"

Before Chen Guiliang could answer, a middle-aged woman at another desk laughed. "Young man, don't be in such a rush to do business. Focus on your foundational courses in your freshman year, get to know more teachers and classmates. When you're a sophomore, with teachers to guide you and classmates as your partners, it won't be too late to start your venture when the conditions are right."

Chen Guiliang took out the simple set of Legends of the Three Kingdoms cards. "You could take a look at this first, ma'am."

"Fine, I suppose you won't listen to advice anyway."

The slightly balding man began to carefully read the business plan and examine the deck of cards.

More than ten minutes later, he said with a smile, "This is a little interesting. Fill out the project application form, leave your things here for now. I can help you submit it; it should pass the incubation review. I'll give you a call then, and you can come over to sign an incubation agreement."

"How long will it probably take?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The man replied, "Fifteen days at the quickest, one or two months at the slowest. You can go ask the Administrative and Logistics Department; they'll tell you what materials to prepare for incubation."

"Thank you, sir. I won't disturb you any longer." Chen Guiliang bowed and left.

The Administrative and Logistics Department was just next door.

This department handled business registration, financial and tax services, and was also responsible for office space allocation, equipment maintenance, and so on.

The staff member who received Chen Guiliang was quite young, much more enthusiastic than the balding middle-aged man from before.

Chen Guiliang quickly explained his situation.

The young staff member took out a pen and paper, had him write down the required materials, and then reminded him, "If you want to sell physical cards, you need to apply for a 'Publication Business License.' Selling without a license is considered dealing in illegal publications."

Chen Guiliang was of course aware of this, but he wasn't clear about the situation in 2004, so he had come to inquire today.

He also asked about the licenses needed to operate online games.

He finally confirmed it: no game publication number was needed!

As long as other business licenses were in order, any game could be launched online, unlike the strict regulations that would come later.

"Can you help me apply for those licenses?" Chen Guiliang asked again.

The young staff member said, "We can, for a service fee."

Chen Guiliang made some more detailed inquiries and found that they could handle almost anything here, and the service fees were very cheap.

The young staff member offered a suggestion: "After you've designed the physical cards, I can help you apply for a trademark and register the copyright. Then you can find a factory to commission the printing. After printing, you can't just sell them without a publication license, but you can find a qualified enterprise to act as your sales agent. Applying for the license yourself is too much trouble; you need a proper warehouse and business premises."

The man didn't spell it out completely, but Chen Guiliang understood.

Before he got the publication license or found an agent, it wouldn't be a big deal to sell a few sets of cards privately on a small scale.

"Thank you for the advice, sir," Chen Guiliang said sincerely.

As long as he successfully entered the Peking University Science Park, he wouldn't even need a physical office. For a 2,000 yuan annual fee, he could register his company at their address. The service also came with three years of complimentary financial and tax assistance.

The Incubation Services Department would track his company's growth and help him apply for policy support when the time was right.

Once the company reached a certain scale, they would even help with connecting him to financing.

If Chen Guiliang's company's annual revenue or profit grew by more than 25% for three consecutive years and met a certain revenue threshold, he could even apply to join Zhongguancun's "Gazelle Program."

Enterprises selected for the Gazelle Program would receive direct government subsidies, bank loan subsidies, and priority investment from partnered venture capital firms. Their corporate income tax would be waived for three years and halved for the next three. They would receive subsidies for attracting high-end talent and be granted Beijing household registration. They could acquire land for R&D or production at preferential prices, and they would receive promotion through official channels.

ByteDance had emerged from the "Gazelle Program."

Chen Guiliang left the Innovation Center and rode his bicycle around.

He looked at the Peking University Science Park, expanding everywhere, hoping these buildings would be constructed quickly. Who knew which one would become his company's office?

Chen Guiliang had arrived at a good time.

This year, the Peking University Science Park was frantically expanding its scale and had also relaxed its entry application requirements.

If he had come last year, it probably would have been much more difficult.
